candidates.expectations: Issuer IR targets about EUR650m 2026 revenue and EUR200m-EUR230m net income, with customer-account growth of at least 10% CAGR and more than 4m customers by end-2027.
candidates.priced_in: The stock closed EUR31.60 on September 11 versus EUR37.74 at first mention, and Reuters reported a 7.9% fall that day after the supervisory-board chairman resigned. Prior optimism has been repriced, but governance uncertainty prevents treating weakness as support.
candidates.bull_case: Strong customer/account and asset growth could keep accelerated 2026 targets achievable; the EUR XETRA listing avoids direct FX conversion for the EUR account.
candidates.bear_case: The chairman resignation adds governance uncertainty, September KPIs may merely meet already-high targets, and the sharp decline may represent thesis deterioration rather than a pullback.
candidates.pre_mortem: The watch fails because leadership change signals broader governance problems while September activity merely meets expectations and price never rebuilds constructive structure.
candidates.red_team_argument: The date, eToro stock availability, core market cap and preferred liquidity survive, but the governance shock and roughly 16% fall from first mention materially weaken the setup; the zero-row canonical snapshot cannot validate structure.

candidates.expectations: Issuer materials say FY2026 net sales and adjusted EBITDA exceeded the high end of guidance. Focus to Win actions are ongoing, so Q1 must show execution can offset international demand and price/mix pressure.
candidates.priced_in: The prior FY2026 beat is known, while dated market history shows a fall from the mid-50s in late August to about USD47. The decline lowers the starting valuation but does not establish support or a reversal setup.
candidates.bull_case: North American execution and Focus to Win savings could sustain the prior guidance-beating trajectory; core market cap and deep liquidity make the name operationally tradeable if structure improves.
candidates.bear_case: International demand weakness, price/mix pressure and restructuring costs can overwhelm North American gains; a falling pre-event tape can continue without forming support.
candidates.pre_mortem: The watch fails because international weakness and restructuring costs dominate Q1 while the pre-event decline never forms a valid base.
candidates.red_team_argument: The October 6 date is primary-source verified and broker/core-cap/liquidity gates pass, but the canonical snapshot has zero rows, the recent tape is falling, and no evidence-based trigger/stop/target can be constructed.
